newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian gold, silver end lower as world prices dip.
newsitem.headline: Indian gold, silver end lower as world prices dip.

text.p: ** Indian gold 22 carat prices close 35 rupees lower at 4,365 rupees per 10 grammes after world prices crashed to their lowest in 12 years, dealers said.
** Prices of gold biscuits end 500 rupees down at 51,000 rupees per piece (116.50 grammes).
** Silver (.999) closes 105 rupees lower at 6,520 rupees per kg, moving in the shadow of gold.
Gold crashed through the barrier of 4,400 rupees per 10 grammes under pressure of a plunge in world prices, dealers said on Friday.
They said silver prices also fell sharply on weak world trends and poor industrial demand.
Standard gold prices fell to 4,365 rupees per 10 grammes from the previous close following its plunge below the $325 per ounce on the London market, dealers said.
"There had been little physical demand for gold despite a fall in prices," said a dealer.
Gold 22 carat also lost 35 rupees to 4,035 rupees per 10 grammes.
Gold biscuit prices (116.50 grammes each) dropped 500 rupees to 51,000 rupees per piece on continued selling pressure from dealers.
Silver (.999) lost 105 rupees to 6,520 rupees per kg due to sluggish industrial demand and weak overseas trends. Raw silver (.916) also slided by the same margin at 6,420 rupees per kg.
